actual_views.observation: Four slanted lines: il faut vérifier la; transitivité crosses the main-line Alors but has tall t strokes and final accented group; de cette relation; c’est immédiat with terminal t. The local note is readable but medial strokes remain crowded.

Arrow letter has a small right loop and open left return on a long vertical. Target capital has stem, upper bar, sloped right bowl and lower return. Suffix begins with long looped f and ends with a high dot/mark above a short terminal; compressed medial strokes leave candidate readings open.

Both Pi forms have a cap and two legs. Underbrace spans the right-hand x<y relation. After i.e. a small crossed older mark is obscured by a zigzag. The annotation gives Sigma-alpha-x intersection Sigma-beta-sigma-y equals slashed oval. This crop contains the targeted old mark and all formula members.
After qu’ two tall l loops lead into a long low final stroke with a downward hook. The hook supports elles but does not securely separate a terminal s from an ending flourish.
Between C and son image the low connector has a small first body, short angled return and open terminal curve. Avec remains visually compressed. A comma follows image.

Non is followed by a long p descender, compressed ana, c/h with tall loop and high accent over the terminal group. A low extra return leaves panaché/panachée open; terminal point is detached. No underline is visible under this word.

Maquette-like word has low initial bodies, a long q descender and two high t strokes. At ordonnée’s beginning older looped material intersects the live start; old de and its exact state remain open. One long underline runs beneath the phrase. Adjacent fini at lower edge is incidental, not the target.

Décompositions begins with a retraced d/é group, then low com, p descent and t followed by ion/s. N-aires includes a long horizontal before the aires group. Both targets and terminal parenthesis are visible.
Fini stands above a cancelled ordonné-like word. The cancellation is a long separate horizontal, while old o/r/d bodies and final accented ending survive. Fini has a tall f and two high dots.
A small sigma-like loop is above the line after involution and a long curved placement stroke descends beside it. The t after p is raised; sans and fixe remain on the main baseline.

The prior line ends ayant la: one looped l and low a without a separately written s. The following propriété/suivante bodies are at the lower edge; the p descender is clipped in this crop. An existing R2 crop was inspected for those lower target words before deciding them.

Three draft lines are crossed. First gives Si x,y in C et x<y, alors x et y. The second comparison has dense crossed material at sigma-x and the relation. Congrus-like body has one obvious g descent; final line contains non congrus mod C, with an open capital C and comma. These letter groups remain partly joined to cancellation.

Full propriété and suivante targets are visible, including the p descender. Each ending has a short final turn without a securely isolated s. A colon follows. This existing second reader crop addresses the target edge left open by R1’s broader line-pair crop; no crop was created again.

Live a/b are joined by a brace. A dense crossed group follows the first C. X,y comparables is raised above cancelled sigma-x,y et x,sigma-y. Three low s-like forms precede sigma-x,y non comparables. The long cancellation starts near b and crosses the older comparables, et sigma-y<sigma-x line, passing above the live lower implication. The live lower implication has a doubled right arrow.

Upper a-like closed body and parenthesis are crossed by a large zigzag; successive b-like and et-like starters are overpainted. The tag beneath crossed material has a 2/8-like group but intersects the slanted margin. Live a) and b) remain to the right of the long brace.

NB is followed by a compressed implique-like word with a tall l loop and long q descent, then que. Compar. ends in a detached point. The arrow has two shafts and a right head joined near the q descent. Non congrus is heavily rewritten where neighbouring strokes intersect. Mod sigma occupies the final line. All target line endings are inside the rotated crop.

Underlined NB begins the last note. Cela is clear; the next overwritten verb has a dense initial group and a long descending q, leaving indique/implique open. Ens has no detached terminal point. The final C is visible above the photographed bottom band; the q descenders touch that source boundary.

The lower target has an angular capital I, low n, looped d, deep p and a long compressed medial continuation. The p descender reaches the crop bottom. The initial and major ascenders are readable, but the compressed medial sequence supports retaining the word uncertainty. Panaché above was already viewed in its own crop; this additional existing crop was selected for the distinct Indépendamment locus.

Both marks have an upper arch and three downward open ends directed toward the lower omega. The clockwise-rotated membership is resolved. H explicitly describes the same vertical layout. The letter below x has two rounded low bowls with raised outer ends and a separate lower alpha. The corresponding beta occurrence repeats that shape. Omega is resolved.

Both point abbreviations have a long p and a smaller crossed t raised to its upper right. The first is confirmed by a new local crop; the second was already visible in R1’s sigma/point crop. Both are preserved as p with raised t.

Il ends the preceding line; the next begins with one long f, separate et and short s with a low point before que. The written abbreviation il f et s. is preserved. The inspected strictement line and the separate non panaché crop show no independent underline under this qualification. H’s emphasis is removed; the word difference is recorded separately. The low ens ending is followed by open space before ordonnés. There is no detached abbreviation point.

Two detached dark points stand after la, one above and slightly right of the other. Both are inside R1’s existing sigma/point crop, which was displayed again specifically for this newly identified punctuation. The colon after suivante is also retained; C, H, R2 and R3 omit the earlier colon.
Un ens consists of two low groups followed by blank separation before the cancelled ordonné. No detached point appears after ens.
The inserted non comparables ends in a low s return and blank space. The detached comma belongs to the cancelled line below, after comparables. H’s comma after the live replacement is omitted.

The older o/r bodies, distinct d upright, low n shoulders and final accent survive a long separate cancellation below fini. Ordonné is resolved with R2/R3 against R1’s retained doubt.
A low e loop and tall crossed t remain separately traceable under the oblique cancellation. Et is resolved with R2/R3 against R1’s retained doubt.

Two detached dark points stand after la, one above and slightly right of the other. Both are inside R1’s existing sigma/point crop, which was displayed again specifically for this newly identified punctuation. The colon after suivante is also retained; C, H, R2 and R3 omit the earlier colon.

A left curved brace/leader joins raised x,y comparables above the cancelled sigma-x,y / x,sigma-y pair. R3’s vertical group with its visible left brace is adopted. C supplies the insertion but omits the brace; H supplies the brace but does not explicitly mark this upper group as inserted. Its separate replacement note concerns non comparables.
